title: Sylvester Stallone Has ‘Millions of Regrets’ About Doing His Own Stunts: ‘I’m An Idiot for Doing That’
content:
ByPayton Turkeltaub

Sylvester Stalloneis opening up about how decades of daredevilry have affected him—and why he considers himself an “idiot” for continuing to do his own stunts year after year.

In a recent interview withFox News Digital, the “Rocky” actor said he has “millions, millions of regrets” about his action career. “I could literally spend a half hour talking about injuries, the amount, not even like one, I’m talking about 30 hours, 30 minutes of just individual ones, because it becomes compounded. I have been injured many, many times, but after ‘Expendables,’ I ended up with nine back operations, three neck fusions. Both shoulders ripped out, eye, you know, all kinds of lens put … it’s been brutal,” he said, adding that he’s never been “quite the same” since the surgeries.

Stallone starred in — and also directed — the action thriller “The Expendables” in 2010 alongside Jason Statham, Mickey Rourke and more. While filming a scene where Stallone got tackled by WWE legend Steve Austin, the stunt went wrong and left Stallone with dislocated shoulders and a fractured neck that required more than seven back surgeries. The “Rambo” actor needed a metal plate inserted into his neck and spinal fusions.

Stallone’s moral of the story is to “let other people do their job.” “Don’t be a stage hawk, or whatever you call it, a showboat. I know a lot of people are thinking about doing stunts … don’t. Don’t. Let the pro do it,” Stallone said. “You cannot beat gravity; when you hit the ground, you lose, and it’s going to come back.”

He continued, “I mean, just ask every football player in the world. So yeah, and people go, ‘Aren’t you proud of them?’ No. I think I’m an idiot for doing that. I’m proud that I broke myself in pieces. Like, duh, no.”

The actor shared a similar piece of advice ahead of the release of his memoir, “The Steps,” last month; Stallone told The New York Times thattreating his bodyin the “masochistic” ways he did came “at a terrible price.” “If I could do it over again, I would say, ‘Let someone else carry the banner and don’t do your own stunts.”
title_zh: 西爾維斯特·史泰龍(Sylvester Stallone)對於自己親自做特技感到「有千萬個遺憾」： 「我真是個傻瓜，這樣做。」
content_zh:
由佩頓·圖克塔布(Payton Turkeltaub)報導

西爾維斯特·史泰龍(Sylvester Stallone)近日談到數十年來的驚險挑戰對他的影響，以及他為何認為自己是個“白癡”，因為年復一年地繼續自己親自完成特技。

在最近接受福克斯新聞數位版(Fox News Digital)的訪問中，這位《洛基》(Rocky)演員表示，他對自己的動作電影生涯有“數以百萬計的遺憾”。“我可以花半小時來談論受傷的事情，數量，不只是一個，我說的是30小時，30分鐘的個別受傷，因為這些都會累積。我受傷的次數非常非常多，但在《敢死隊》(The Expendables)之後，我做了九次背部手術，三次頸部融合手術。兩肩脫臼，眼睛，知道的，各種鏡頭都放進去……這真是殘酷，”他說，並補充道，自從手術後他就再也“不是同一個人”了。

史泰龍在2010年主演並執導了動作驚悚片《敢死隊》(The Expendables)，與傑森·史塔森(Jason Statham)、米基·洛克(Mickey Rourke)等人合作。在拍攝一個場景時，史泰龍被WWE傳奇史蒂夫·奧斯汀(Steve Austin)摔倒，特技出現意外，導致他肩膀脫臼和頸部骨折，這需要超過七次背部手術。這位《藍波》(Rambo)演員需要在頸部植入金屬板並進行脊椎融合手術。

史泰龍的故事教訓是“讓其他人做他們的工作”。“不要當舞台上的鷹，或者你稱之為的，表演者。我知道很多人想要做特技……不要。不要。讓專業人士來做，”史泰龍說。“你無法戰勝重力；當你摔到地上時，你就輸了，這會回來找你。”

他接著說：“我的意思是，問問全世界的每一位足球運動員。所以是的，人們會說，‘你不為他們感到驕傲嗎？’不。我覺得我這樣做是個白癡。我為自己把自己弄得粉碎而感到驕傲。就像，呃，不。”

這位演員在上個月發行自傳《步伐》(The Steps)之前分享了類似的建議；史泰龍告訴《紐約時報》(The New York Times)，以“自虐”的方式對待自己的身體是“付出了可怕的代價”。“如果我能重新來過，我會說，‘讓其他人扛起旗幟，不要自己做特技。’”
